_comment: Per-object size limits for unit test modules. See
notes/plans/test-module-size-gate-plan.md for the design and
src/utests/AGENTS.md for what to do when a module gets close.
Keys are glob patterns matched against the build directory name,
which is OS-ARCH-TOOLCHAIN-VARIANT. The MOST SPECIFIC pattern wins,
measured by the number of non-wildcard characters.
gate: enforce - over ceiling fails the build
report  - print the line, never fail
off     - silent
ROLLOUT STAGE 0: win-x86 debug only.
That is narrower than 'Windows x86' on purpose. The 75MB ceiling was
calibrated against a 32-bit clang-cl crash on a debug object, and the
2026-09-14 matrix measured win-x86-vc143-release at 96.77MB - above 75,
and building perfectly well. Object size is a proxy for peak compiler
memory, and the proxy is only calibrated for debug. Enforcing 75 across
both variants would fail a build that has never had a problem.
So release is measured but not limited until a number is argued from its
own data. Everything outside win-x86 is off: Linux and macOS objects have
never been measured here at all, and a gate with guessed numbers fires
spuriously, and a gate that fires spuriously gets switched off for good.

win-x86-*-debug.why: 32-bit toolchain, ~2GB address space. The one ceiling calibrated against a real failure: clang-cl 16 died with 0xC000001D on a 112.68MB object. Measured peak after the split is 72.26MB (vc143) and 74.33MB (ccl16).

win-x86-*-release.why: Measured 96.77MB (vc143) and 35.69MB (ccl16) on 2026-09-14, so vc143 release is already well over the debug ceiling and builds fine. Reports against the debug numbers only to make the gap visible; needs its own limit argued before it can enforce.

*.why: Stage 0. win-a64 and win-x64 move to report at stage 1, then enforce at stage 2. Linux and macOS have never been measured.
